case_name: Shri N.C. Jain vs Union Of India And Anr.
facts_of_case: Petitioner was appointed as a Director (Marketing) by respondent No.2/Cement Corporation of India. He submitted his resignation letter dated 27.10.1995 and claimed that since no disciplinary proceedings were pending, his jural relationship as an employee came to an end on the same date.

legal_principles.principle: Harmonious construction of all clauses/terms is necessary.
legal_principles.held: There has to be harmonious construction of all the clauses/terms of the appointment letter dated 14.12.1994.

legal_principles.principle: Automatic resignation cannot be inferred without acceptance by the employer.
legal_principles.held: The resignation is not automatic and government/respondent No.2 has a right to reject the resignation if the circumstances so warrant.

legal_principles.principle: Burden lies on the employee to prove that circumstances warrant rejection of resignation.
legal_principles.held: The burden lies on the petitioner to show that the circumstances are such that the government/respondent No.2 should reject the resignation.

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for quashing chargesheet
assisting in drafting an appointment letter
